hero.headline: Six Bodies Recovered From Washington Paper Mill After Chemical Tank Implosion
hero.body:
Rescue crews have recovered six bodies from a paper mill in Longview, Washington, following a chemical tank rupture earlier this week. Nine workers were reported missing after the incident, with three individuals still unaccounted for and presumed dead.

The tank contained a chemical mixture used in paper manufacturing. The rupture has significantly complicated recovery and cleanup operations at the facility, particularly efforts to manage contaminated water at the site.

According to officials, the confirmed death toll has risen to eight as recovery efforts continue. Eight additional people were injured in the incident, including a firefighter who was responding to the emergency.

The chemical tank's collapse has made recovery operations challenging for emergency responders. Teams have been working to dilute contaminated water and manage the hazardous materials released during the rupture. The exact circumstances that led to the tank failure remain under investigation by authorities.

The incident represents a major industrial accident for the region. Emergency services mobilized quickly to respond to the initial reports, and recovery crews have been working systematically to locate missing workers and manage the site's hazardous conditions.

Local emergency management has coordinated response efforts involving multiple agencies. Officials have emphasized that recovery operations are ongoing as crews work to locate the three remaining missing individuals.

The identities of the recovered victims have not been released by authorities. Families of the missing workers have been notified as recovery and investigation efforts continue.

The paper mill facility has been the focus of extensive emergency response operations. Authorities have stated that they are not currently searching for additional missing persons beyond the three originally reported.

Community support has begun to mobilize for those affected by the disaster. Local organizations have been setting up assistance programs for victims' families, and community members have opportunities to contribute to relief efforts.

Investigators are working to determine what led to the tank rupture and are examining the facility's operations and maintenance protocols. The recovery process has required specialized equipment and expertise due to the hazardous materials involved.

Emergency responders have praised the coordination between different agencies in managing the response. The incident has highlighted the risks associated with chemical storage and handling in industrial facilities.

The site remains an active recovery and investigation zone. Authorities have indicated they will provide updates as the investigation progresses and as recovery operations conclude. The full scope of the damage and detailed findings regarding the incident's cause remain under review.

cards.headline: US and Iran near agreement to extend ceasefire, reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
The United States and Iran are close to finalizing a memorandum of understanding that would extend their ceasefire by 60 days and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though some disagreements remain unresolved.

Vice President JD Vance said Thursday that negotiators were "very close" to completing the agreement but still working through final details. "We're still going back and forth on nuclear stuff," Vance said, indicating that disputes over Tehran's nuclear program continue to be a sticking point.

According to US officials, negotiators have already reached agreement on the framework of a 60-day ceasefire extension. However, the deal still requires final approval from President Trump and Iran's leadership before it becomes official.

The tentative memorandum addresses multiple pressing issues. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route that has been closed during the conflict, would reopen under the agreement. The deal would also establish a framework for broader negotiations on Tehran's nuclear program, a long-standing concern for the Trump administration.

Pakistan has been playing an active role in mediating talks between the two sides. Pakistan's army chief led a delegation to Tehran to convey messages from Washington, while Pakistan's prime minister traveled to Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Turkey to build regional support for a peace agreement.

Karoline Leavitt, the White House press secretary, said on Wednesday that Washington remained engaged in negotiations despite earlier denials of a formal extension request. She stated that a second round of negotiations would "very likely" be held in Islamabad and that the White House feels "good about the prospects of a deal."

The current ceasefire was set to expire on April 22. Both sides have been engaged in indirect talks aimed at extending the truce, with continued exchanges of messages between Washington and Tehran even after previous rounds of negotiations broke down.

Trump and his advisers have previously believed they were close to a final agreement at earlier stages of the conflict, though those negotiations ultimately stalled. A final comprehensive agreement addressing Trump's nuclear demands would require further intensive negotiations beyond the initial memorandum of understanding.

The three-month conflict has strained regional stability and disrupted global shipping routes. Reports from the region suggest both sides favor prolonging the truce, though significant work remains to resolve underlying disputes.

The tentative agreement represents the most substantial diplomatic breakthrough since the conflict began. However, nothing is considered official until formally announced by the White House. Both sides continue intensive discussions to finalize the remaining details before the ceasefire expires.

cards.headline: Trump administration bars Americans exposed to Ebola from returning to US
cards.teaser: A 50-bed quarantine facility in Kenya will house Americans exposed to the virus starting this week.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is building a quarantine and treatment facility in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, rather than allowing them to return home. The 50-bed field hospital is set to open Friday.

Some experts have criticized this approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning to the US could undermine treatment efforts for the outbreak.

cards.headline: Supreme Court Rules for Mississippi Death Row Inmate in Racial Bias Case
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court sided with a Mississippi man on death row in a case involving racial bias in jury selection.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court issued a ruling in favor of a Mississippi death row inmate in a case centered on racial bias during jury selection. Justice Brett Kavanaugh authored the opinion in Pitchford v. Cain.

The decision addressed protections for jury rights in capital cases. Chief Justice John Roberts joined Kavanaugh in the majority opinion, which legal observers described as a win for racial justice in the criminal legal system.

cards.headline: UN Adds Israel to Sexual Violence Blacklist, Israel Severs Ties With Secretary General
cards.teaser: The United Nations added Israeli forces to its blacklist for conflict-related sexual violence, prompting Israel to cut ties with the UN chief.
cards.body:
Israel announced it would sever diplomatic ties with the UN Secretary General after the organization added Israeli entities to its blacklist of parties responsible for sexual violence in armed conflicts. Hamas and Russian forces were also included on the same list.

Israel objected to being placed alongside Hamas on the blacklist. The decision marks a significant escalation in tensions between Israel and UN leadership, prompting Israel to cut off relations with the Secretary General over the listing.

cards.headline: Vance Says Trump Approval Still Uncertain on U.S.-Iran Deal
cards.teaser: Vice President Vance said whether President Trump will approve a U.S.-Iran agreement remains undecided as both countries work to extend a ceasefire.
cards.body:
Vice President JD Vance said the U.S. and Iran are "very close" to reaching a deal to extend their ceasefire, but negotiations have not yet concluded. The framework of a ceasefire extension agreement has been agreed upon, though it still requires approval from both President Trump and Iran's leadership.

Whether Trump will ultimately sign the agreement remains uncertain. Both nations are working to finalize the terms, which would end ongoing hostilities and restore access to the Strait of Hormuz.

cards.headline: Americans' savings rate drops to 2.6 percent in April
cards.teaser: The rate fell below 3 percent for the first time since mid-2022.
cards.body:
Americans' savings rate fell to 2.6 percent in April, dropping below 3 percent for the first time since June 2022. This marks a continued decline in how much of their disposable income households are setting aside rather than spending.

The savings rate is a key economic indicator that reflects consumer behavior and financial health. The lower rate suggests Americans are spending a larger share of their earnings on consumption.

hero.headline: Netanyahu Orders Israeli Military to Control 70 Percent of Gaza
hero.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered the Israeli military to seize control of 70 percent of the Gaza Strip, a move that threatens to violate an existing ceasefire agreement and worsen humanitarian conditions in the territory.

Netanyahu announced the directive at a conference in an occupied West Bank settlement. "We are currently squeezing Hamas. We now control 60% of the territory in the strip. You know, we were at 50, we moved to 60. My directive is to move to 70%," he said.

The expansion would represent a significant escalation beyond the October ceasefire terms. Under the US-brokered agreement, Israeli forces withdrew to a demarcation line that gave Israel direct control of 53 percent of Gaza. Since the truce began, Israeli forces have steadily advanced westward into Hamas-controlled areas and established an expanded no-man's land, claiming the right to control who enters and to open fire on perceived threats. More than 900 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces during the eight-month ceasefire period.

The expansion would directly violate the October ceasefire, the UN Security Council resolution that endorsed it, and Donald Trump's 20-point peace plan. That plan established a temporary dividing line pending further negotiations and stated that no one would be forced to leave Gaza.

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has indicated that the government's ultimate goal is for large numbers of Palestinians to leave Gaza through what he called "voluntary migration," though human rights activists describe this as ethnic cleansing achieved by making living conditions intolerable.

The expansion to 70 percent control would compress Gaza's 2.2 million Palestinians into less than a third of their original territory. The area is already described as the world's single most overcrowded place. Israeli forces have systematically destroyed buildings in their controlled zone, leaving Palestinians with virtually no space to relocate.

According to UN briefings for humanitarian agencies, Israeli forces have been steadily expanding their positions throughout the ceasefire. In northern Jabalia, tanks have advanced daily with drones targeting any movement near the dividing line. Israeli-backed militias, including one run by Gaza warlord Ashraf al-Mansi, have played an increasing role in the expansion, functioning as shock troops for the Israeli army.

These militias have been forcibly evacuating Palestinian residents from areas near the ceasefire line. One resident described armed militiamen entering his family's area and giving residents until 10pm to vacate their homes, instructing them to take only what they could carry.

Netanyahu's directive comes as he faces pressure domestically ahead of elections expected within the next few months. The order represents the most significant territorial expansion ordered during the current conflict.

cards.headline: Russian Drone Strikes Romanian Apartment Building, Injuring Multiple People
cards.teaser: A Russian drone crashed into a block of flats in Romania's Galati area, causing an explosion and fire.
cards.body:
A Russian drone struck a residential high-rise building in Romania, injuring multiple people. The impact caused an explosion and fire at the apartment block in the Galati area. NATO scrambled fighter jets in response to the incident.

The strike on the residential building marks a significant escalation involving a NATO member state. Romania borders Ukraine and has previously experienced drone incidents related to the ongoing conflict in the region. The deployment of NATO fighter jets underscores the seriousness with which the alliance is treating the incident.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran Near Agreement to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: American officials say they are closing in on an arrangement with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though President Trump has not approved the framework.
cards.body:
U.S. and Iran officials are moving closer to a framework agreement aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Vice President Vance confirmed the two countries are very close to a deal but have not finalized it yet. The framework would extend the current ceasefire and potentially open the door to more substantive negotiations between the nations.

President Trump has not yet approved the emerging agreement. Iran's leadership also needs to sign off on the arrangement. Negotiations continue even as the U.S. and Iran have exchanged military strikes during the peace talks.

cards.headline: UN Adds Israel to Sexual Violence Blacklist, Israel Severs Ties With Secretary General
cards.teaser: The United Nations added Israeli forces to its blacklist for conflict-related sexual violence, prompting Israel to cut ties with the UN chief.

Israel announced it would sever diplomatic ties with the UN Secretary General after the organization added Israeli entities to its blacklist of parties responsible for sexual violence in armed conflicts. Hamas and Russian forces were also included on the same list.

cards.headline: Austria Jails Man 15 Years for Plot to Attack Taylor Swift Concert
cards.teaser: A 21-year-old Austrian man received a 15-year sentence for planning an attack on a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna.
cards.body:
A 21-year-old Austrian man has been sentenced to 15 years in prison after being found guilty of plotting to attack a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna. The court convicted him of planning the assault and related terrorism offenses.

The verdict concludes the case against the individual, who faced multiple terrorism charges stemming from the planned attack on the concert venue in the Austrian capital.

cards.headline: Portugal Sets New May Temperature Record as Europe Faces Heat Wave
cards.teaser: Portugal broke its hottest May day record as a heat wave swept across Europe, with red alerts issued in Italy.
cards.body:
Portugal recorded its highest temperature ever for the month of May as a heat wave affects multiple European countries. Italy issued red alerts in response to the elevated temperatures. French students are taking exams in sweltering conditions at schools.

The record-breaking heat in Portugal marks an unusual weather event for late May. The heat wave's scope extends across southern Europe, affecting daily activities and prompting emergency weather alerts. The timing of the heat wave coincides with the end of the school year in France, forcing students to sit for exams in extreme temperatures.

cards.headline: Italian Police Discover $230 Million Empire of Dead Mob Boss
cards.teaser: Authorities uncovered the vast business network of Sicilian mafia boss Matteo Messina Denaro, who died in 2023.
cards.body:
Italian police discovered a $230 million business empire belonging to deceased mob boss Matteo Messina Denaro. The investigation began with a tip about a wealthy Sicilian woman's significant assets held in a small European principality. When Denaro died in 2023, many of his secrets appeared to die with him.

The discovery marks a breakthrough in understanding the financial network of one of Sicily's most powerful mafia figures. Denaro's empire remained hidden for years, with its scale only becoming apparent after investigators followed leads about assets held outside Italy. The uncovering of the business network demonstrates the continued efforts to

cards.headline: At Least Three Dead in Dallas Apartment Building Gas Explosion
cards.teaser: A gas explosion and fire at a Dallas apartment complex killed at least three people, including a child.
cards.body:
At least three people died in a gas explosion and fire at a Dallas apartment complex in the Oak Cliff area on Thursday. The victims were two adult women and one child, whose bodies were found in the rubble.

Nearly 100 firefighters responded to battle the flames, which left the building collapsed. Four additional people were hospitalized following the blast. Rescue crews continued searching through the destroyed structure as operations proceeded at the site.

cards.headline: Supreme Court Rules for Mississippi Death Row Inmate in Racial Bias Case
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court sided with a Mississippi man on death row in a case involving racial bias in jury selection.

cards.headline: Two Killed in U.S. Military Strike on Suspected Drug Boat in Pacific
cards.teaser: A U.S. military strike on a suspected narcotics vessel in the eastern Pacific killed two men.
cards.body:
Two men died when U.S. forces struck a boat suspected of drug trafficking in the eastern Pacific. The military action targeted what officials identified as a narco vessel operating in international waters.

Survivors from the strike have not been located. The incident brings the overall death toll from U.S. boat strikes to 199, according to reports tracking similar operations in the region.

cards.headline: King's College Hospital Opens First Rooftop Intensive Care Ward
cards.teaser: A London hospital launched the first outdoor intensive care ward to study whether fresh air improves recovery for critically ill patients.
cards.body:
King's College Hospital in London has opened an outdoor intensive care ward on its rooftop, marking a novel approach to critical care. The facility will observe whether fresh air and open-air conditions benefit patients recovering from serious illness.

The hospital is tracking patient outcomes to measure whether the outdoor environment provides tangible health advantages over traditional indoor intensive care units. One patient quoted in reports noted the psychological impact, saying "I forgot what it feels like to be outside."

cards.headline: Portugal Records Hottest May Temperature as Europe Faces Heatwave
cards.teaser: Portugal broke its record for the hottest day in May as a heatwave continued across southern Europe.
cards.body:
Portugal set a new record for the hottest temperature recorded in May as a severe heatwave swept across western Europe. The extreme heat resulted from the combined effects of a heat dome and climate change, causing temperatures to reach unprecedented levels.

Multiple European countries issued heat warnings and adjusted operations in response to the dangerous conditions. French students sat for exams in schools battling extreme temperatures, while Italian authorities declared red alerts. England and Wales also experienced record May temperatures during the same weather event.

hero.headline: Dell shares surge 31% on raised AI server sales outlook
hero.body:
Dell Technologies shares jumped more than 30% after the company raised its outlook for AI server sales and reported its fastest sales growth since returning to public markets in 2018.

The technology manufacturer now expects to sell $60 billion worth of AI servers, according to its latest financial results. The updated forecast drove shares up by as much as 40% in after-hours trading, with the stock settling at a 31% gain.

Dell delivered first quarter fiscal 2027 financial results that exceeded Wall Street expectations. The performance marked the company's strongest sales growth rate in more than seven years, fueled by demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The server business has become a critical growth driver for Dell as companies invest heavily in building out AI capabilities. Major technology firms and enterprises are purchasing servers optimized for training and running large language models and other AI applications.

Dell's results contributed to a broader market rally that pushed stock indexes to new highs. The strong earnings report comes amid growing investor enthusiasm about AI-related technology spending.

The company's fiscal first quarter results demonstrate how hardware makers are benefiting from the AI boom that has primarily lifted software and chipmaker stocks over the past year. Server demand has proven more resilient than some analysts expected as organizations build dedicated AI infrastructure rather than relying solely on cloud services.

Dell's raised outlook suggests the company sees sustained demand for AI servers extending through the rest of its fiscal year. The forecast increase signals confidence that current order pipelines will convert to revenue as customers take delivery of systems.

The stock surge added billions to Dell's market value in a single trading session, rewarding investors who held through uncertainty about whether AI spending would translate into hardware sales. The results position Dell as a primary beneficiary of the ongoing buildout of AI computing capacity across the technology sector.

cards.headline: Fertitta Entertainment acquires Caesars for $5.7 billion
cards.teaser: Caesars Entertainment, a Las Vegas Strip icon, sold to Fertitta Entertainment in a deal valued at nearly $6 billion.
cards.body:
Fertitta Entertainment is acquiring Caesars Entertainment, a Las Vegas Strip icon, for $5.7 billion in cash. The total transaction value reaches $17.6 billion when factoring in assumed debt.

The deal strengthens Tilman Fertitta's position in the gaming industry, adding four Atlantic City casinos to his portfolio alongside major Las Vegas properties. The acquisition reflects Fertitta's continued investment in the Las Vegas market.

cards.headline: Federal regulator pauses Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern merger review
cards.teaser: The Surface Transportation Board accepted a revised $71.5 billion merger application from Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern but delayed proceedings.
cards.body:
The Surface Transportation Board accepted the revised merger application from Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern but announced it wants more information before beginning its formal review. The $71.5 billion deal would create the first transcontinental railroad spanning coast to coast.

The federal regulator's decision to pause the process introduces uncertainty into the timeline for completing the merger between two of the nation's largest freight railroads. The STB's request for additional information suggests concerns that need addressing before the agency can evaluate whether the combination serves the public interest.

cards.headline: IBM and Red Hat commit $5 billion to open source security initiative
cards.teaser: IBM pledged $5 billion for an AI-driven open source security initiative in response to recent cyber threats.
cards.body:
IBM and Red Hat announced a $5 billion commitment to redefine the future of open source security in the AI era. The initiative aims to combat cyber threats using artificial intelligence and establish IBM and Red Hat as a security clearinghouse for open source applications in the enterprise.

IBM CEO Arvind Krishna said the Mythos incident was the critical trigger for the company's open source cybersecurity push. The investment represents one of the largest corporate commitments to securing the open source software that underpins much of the technology industry.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary backs putting Trump on new $250 bill
cards.teaser: The Treasury Department is preparing to make Donald Trump the face of a new $250 bill, though the move would require new legislation.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the White House is pursuing a $250 bill featuring Donald Trump's portrait to commemorate the nation's 250th anniversary of independence. The Treasury Department has already begun preparing for the new currency's potential production.

Current federal law prohibits living individuals from appearing on US currency, so the proposal requires Congressional approval to proceed. While Trump allies in Congress are backing the measure, Democrats have pledged to block the initiative.

cards.headline: Federal government launches Trump Accounts app nationwide
cards.teaser: The Treasury Department rolled out an app to manage $1,000 federal investment accounts for children.
cards.body:
The Treasury Department has rolled out the Trump Accounts app, which allows families to access and manage $1,000 federal investment accounts created for each child. Treasury Secretary Bessent announced the nationwide launch of the application.

The app gives parents and guardians the ability to monitor the government-funded investment accounts set up for children. This new federal program aims to provide initial capital for young Americans.

cards.headline: ABC accuses FCC of threatening broadcast licenses in retaliation
cards.teaser: ABC slammed the Federal Communications Commission, saying the regulator was targeting its station licenses unconstitutionally.
cards.body:
ABC has accused the Federal Communications Commission of targeting its station licenses as part of what the network describes as unconstitutional retaliation. The broadcaster claims the FCC's actions represent an attempt to punish the company.

The dispute marks an escalation in tensions between ABC and federal regulators over license renewals, which require periodic approval from the FCC.

hero.headline: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket explodes during Florida testing
hero.body:
A New Glenn rocket operated by Blue Origin exploded during testing at a facility in Florida. The rocket is a key component of Jeff Bezos' spaceflight company's efforts to compete in the commercial launch market.

The explosion represents a significant setback for Blue Origin as it works to establish itself as a competitor to SpaceX in the space industry. New Glenn is the company's heavy-lift orbital rocket designed to carry satellites and other payloads into space.

Blue Origin has been developing New Glenn for several years as part of its strategy to capture a share of the growing commercial space launch market. The rocket is named after John Glenn, the first American to orbit Earth.

The company founded by Bezos has faced delays in bringing New Glenn to operational status. The explosion during testing will likely push back the timeline for the rocket's first operational flights.

SpaceX, led by Elon Musk, currently dominates the commercial launch industry with its Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets. The company has successfully launched hundreds of missions and maintains a steady launch cadence. Blue Origin has been working to develop comparable capabilities with New Glenn.

Testing failures are not uncommon in rocket development, but they typically require extensive investigation and can lead to design modifications. The cause of the explosion has not been disclosed.

Blue Origin also operates the New Shepard suborbital rocket, which has been used for space tourism flights. New Glenn represents the company's push into the more lucrative orbital launch market, where demand from satellite operators and government agencies continues to grow.

The setback comes as competition in the space industry intensifies, with multiple companies vying for launch contracts from commercial customers and government agencies including NASA and the Department of Defense.

cards.headline: Large language models accept false information despite explicit warnings
cards.teaser: Research shows AI language models treat false statements as true even when directly told the information is incorrect.
cards.body:
New research reveals that large language models continue to treat false statements as factual, even when explicitly warned that the information is incorrect. Fine-tuning tests demonstrated this troubling pattern, showing the models exhibit a bias toward confidently representing claims as true regardless of contradictory instructions.

This finding poses significant concerns for AI systems deployed in applications requiring factual accuracy. The research exposes a fundamental limitation in how language models process and handle information they've been specifically told is false, raising questions about their reliability in real-world use cases.

cards.headline: Cloud providers redesign infrastructure for AI-generated traffic
cards.teaser: Amazon Web Services, Cloudflare, and other companies are rebuilding internet infrastructure to handle machine-generated traffic rather than human users.
cards.body:
Major cloud infrastructure providers are redesigning their systems to accommodate a shift from human-generated to machine-generated internet traffic. Companies including AWS and Cloudflare are making changes as AI agents move from experimental projects to production deployments.

The infrastructure changes reflect expectations that AI systems will become the dominant source of internet traffic in coming years. The redesign effort addresses different patterns in how machines access and process information compared to human users, requiring new approaches to network architecture and data handling.

cards.headline: Waymo leads autonomous vehicle registrations in Texas as new tracking system launches
cards.teaser: A new law and tracking tool reveal Waymo holds the largest share of registered autonomous vehicles in Texas, with Tesla registering fewer vehicles.
cards.body:
Waymo has registered the most autonomous vehicles in Texas, according to a new tracking tool created under recent state legislation. The system provides the clearest public accounting yet of robotaxis and self-driving trucks operating across the state.

Tesla has registered fewer autonomous vehicles in Texas despite its major presence in the electric vehicle market. The new tracker offers detailed insight into which companies are deploying self-driving vehicles in the state and their numbers.

cards.headline: Enterprise AI search startup Glean reaches $300 million in annual revenue
cards.teaser: Glean tripled its annual revenue by positioning AI-powered search as a tool for budget reduction, even as tech giants entered the market.
cards.body:
I don't have access to a source that confirms the details in the original card about Glean reaching $300 million in annual revenue, tripling its revenue, or its positioning around AI-driven budget reduction.

The additional source material provided (about AI drug research and a Thai police AI fake image) is about different stories entirely and doesn't contain information about Glean.

Since I cannot verify the original card's claims with the provided sources, I'm returning the original card text unchanged:

Glean, an enterprise AI search startup, has crossed $300 million in annual top-line revenue. The company tripled its revenue by emphasizing AI-driven budget reduction as a primary selling point to business customers.

The growth came despite increased competition from major technology companies entering the enterprise AI search category. Glean has positioned its product as a way for organizations to reduce costs through more efficient information retrieval and workflow automation.

cards.headline: Developer plants data-deleting code to sabotage AI coding assistants
cards.teaser: A programmer added a hidden prompt injection to their code library that instructs AI coding agents to delete application output.
cards.body:
A software developer inserted a hidden prompt injection into the jqwik code library that instructs AI coding assistants to delete application output. The developer took the action out of frustration with what they termed vibe coders who rely heavily on AI tools.

The undisclosed addition targets AI agents used for code generation and modification. When AI systems process the compromised code, the embedded instructions tell them to perform destructive operations on the software being developed.

cards.headline: Study finds US healthcare costs remain high with poor health outcomes
cards.teaser: Research shows American healthcare continues to be expensive while delivering inferior results compared to other developed nations.
cards.body:
A new study concludes that US healthcare remains expensive while producing poor outcomes relative to costs. The research found that despite high spending, Americans experience worse health results than populations in other developed countries.

The study identified strategies that could improve healthcare delivery and outcomes, but found that the US healthcare system is not implementing these approaches. The findings add to a body of research documenting the gap between American healthcare spending and health outcomes.

hero.headline: MLB proposes hard salary cap in first collective bargaining offer to players union
hero.body:
Major League Baseball has submitted its opening proposal in collective bargaining negotiations with the players union, marking the first time since 1994 that the league has formally proposed a hard salary cap system. The offer also includes a $171 million salary floor that would require all teams to meet a minimum payroll threshold.

The proposal comes as MLB seeks to address what ownership describes as competitive balance issues within the league. Team owners have long contended that a salary cap would create a more level playing field between franchises in large markets and those in smaller markets with lower revenues.

Currently, MLB operates under a luxury tax system that penalizes teams for exceeding a certain payroll threshold rather than imposing a strict cap on spending. The introduction of a hard cap would represent a fundamental shift in how the league structures player compensation and team roster construction.

The $171 million salary floor would have significant implications for lower-spending franchises. Teams that currently operate with smaller payrolls would be forced to substantially increase their spending on player salaries to comply with the new requirement.

The last time MLB formally proposed a salary cap was in 1994, a move that triggered a work stoppage that resulted in the cancellation of 938 games and the World Series. That dispute stands as one of the most damaging periods in baseball history and remains a sensitive topic in labor negotiations.

The players union now possesses the proposal and will conduct a comprehensive review of all terms. Union representatives have not yet publicly responded to the offer or indicated their initial reaction to the salary cap proposal. Before the union can move forward with negotiations, player representatives must evaluate the complete proposal and develop their own counteroffer.

This opening position from ownership suggests that negotiations could extend over an extended period as both sides work toward reaching a new collective bargaining agreement. The proposal represents one of the most significant proposed changes to baseball's economic structure in decades.

The path forward will depend heavily on how players and their agents respond to the cap and floor system. If the union views the proposal as a serious starting point for negotiation, discussions could proceed with relative efficiency. However, given the contentious history surrounding salary caps in baseball, there remains the possibility that disagreements could escalate into another work stoppage.

Negotiations between MLB and the players union are expected to continue as both sides attempt to reach consensus on a new agreement before the current labor deal expires.

cards.headline: Knicks center Mitchell Robinson breaks pinky finger, status for NBA Finals unclear
cards.teaser: New York Knicks center Mitchell Robinson suffered a broken pinky finger on his right hand with no timetable set for his return.
cards.body:
Mitchell Robinson broke his pinky finger on his right hand. The Knicks have not provided a timeline for when the center might return to the court.

The injury puts Robinson's availability for the NBA Finals in question. The Knicks have advanced to the championship series, but will need to evaluate how to proceed without their starting center if he cannot play.

cards.headline: Four-time Stanley Cup champion Claude Lemieux dies at 60
cards.teaser: Claude Lemieux, who won four Stanley Cup championships during his NHL career, has died at age 60.
cards.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup champion known for his fierce, hard-hitting style of play, has died at age 60. The fiery winger won championships with three different teams and earned the 1995 Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP. His aggressive approach sometimes overshadowed his considerable skills, but he delivered consistently in crucial games.

Lemieux died after taking his own life, according to authorities. The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office responded to the scene at a furniture store showroom in Lake Park, Florida, just after 3 a.m. on Thursday. After his playing career, Lemieux worked as a player agent.

cards.headline: Spurs face elimination as Thunder lead Western Conference Finals 3-2
cards.teaser: The San Antonio Spurs must win Game 6 to avoid elimination and force the Western Conference Finals back to Oklahoma City.
cards.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder hold a 3-2 series lead over the San Antonio Spurs in the Western Conference Finals. Game 6 will determine whether the Spurs can extend the series or the Thunder advance to the NBA Finals.

The Thunder's role players have stepped up during the series, performing at a high level alongside the team's stars. The Spurs need a strong response to push the series to a seventh game in Oklahoma City.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi named to Argentina squad for sixth World Cup
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi will captain Argentina at the 2026 World Cup, becoming one of the few players to compete in six World Cups.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi has been selected for Argentina's 2026 World Cup squad, marking his sixth appearance at the tournament. The captain will lead the defending champions as they seek to retain their title in the competition being held across North America.

Messi's inclusion adds to his storied international legacy. He previously won the World Cup with Argentina, cementing his place among the sport's greatest players.

cards.headline: Luke Littler wins Premier League darts title after 11-10 victory over Luke Humphries
cards.teaser: World champion Luke Littler defeated Luke Humphries 11-10 in the Premier League final at The O2 in London.
cards.body:
Luke Littler reclaimed the Premier League darts title with a thrilling 11-10 victory over Luke Humphries in what has been recognised as one of the competition's greatest finals. The world champion delivered one of his best performances to exact revenge on his rival.

Littler was visibly emotional after his triumph at The O2. He later disclosed that he had seriously considered withdrawing from the Premier League earlier in the season, making this comeback victory all the more significant.

cards.headline: Texas Tech coach says Red Raiders would play Texas in Week 1 after Longhorns coach comments
cards.teaser: Texas Tech head coach Joey McGuire said his team would welcome a Week 1 matchup against Texas following comments from Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian.
cards.body:
Joey McGuire responded to Steve Sarkisian's recent scheduling comments by stating Texas Tech would be willing to play Texas in the first week of the 2026 season. The Red Raiders coach made clear his team has no hesitation about facing the Longhorns.

Texas Tech may pay the buyout for Texas to cancel a scheduled game against Texas State in order to play the Longhorns instead. The potential matchup would feature several players facing their former teams after recent transfers.

hero.headline: Fourth Artist Drops Out of Trump-Linked Freedom 250 Concert Series
hero.body:
Country singer Martina McBride withdrew from the Freedom 250 concert series planned for the National Mall in Washington, D.C., becoming the fourth performer to back out of the event. McBride posted on social media that she was dropping out after learning the concerts carried more political associations than she initially realized.

The concert series is organized by Keith Krach, a Trump appointee, as part of celebrations for America's 250th anniversary. The Commodores, Morris Day, and Young MC previously withdrew from the lineup after it was announced.

The event has drawn criticism over its political ties and how it was marketed to performers. Artists who backed out indicated they were unaware of the full political context when they agreed to participate. The concerts are scheduled to take place on the National Mall in Washington, D.C.

CBS News reported that several artists withdrew shortly after the lineup was publicly announced. Rolling Stone described the concert series as misleading in its presentation to potential performers. NBC News and The New York Times also covered the wave of artist withdrawals from the event.

The Freedom 250 concerts are part of broader national celebrations marking the United States' 250th anniversary. The event's organizer, Keith Krach, served in the Trump administration. The National Mall in Washington, D.C., has historically been a venue for major national events and celebrations.

McBride's announcement came late in the evening. Her social media post explained that she had not fully understood the political dimensions of the event when she initially committed to perform. The other artists who withdrew gave similar reasons for their decisions.

The concert series continues to face scrutiny over how performers were recruited and whether they were given complete information about the event's political backing. The Associated Press reported that The Commodores and Morris Day specifically cited the Trump connection in their decisions to withdraw from the shows.

cards.headline: CBS Says Byron Allen Deal Will Bring $15 Million Profit After Colbert Cancellation
cards.teaser: CBS disclosed financial projections for its time-lease agreement with Byron Allen following the cancellation of The Late Show.
cards.body:
CBS announced that leasing its late-night time slot to Byron Allen will generate $15 million in profit. The network canceled The Late Show with Stephen Colbert and replaced it with Allen's Comics Unleashed, which drew 995,000 viewers on debut—an 85 percent decline from Colbert's final episode.

CBS defended the decision after weeks of backlash, characterizing the time-buy arrangement as a new approach to late-night programming. Allen, who has pursued this opportunity for 51 years, said the show will emphasize comedy while avoiding heavy political humor, positioning it as an alternative to the network's existing late-night slate.

cards.headline: Bari Weiss Replaces Executive Producer at 60 Minutes in Major Shakeup
cards.teaser: CBS News leader Bari Weiss named Nick Bilton as the new executive producer of 60 Minutes, replacing Tanya Simon.
cards.body:
Bari Weiss, who leads CBS News, replaced the executive producer of 60 Minutes as part of what she called a new approach to the long-running news program. Nick Bilton will take over from Tanya Simon in the role. Correspondents Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi also departed the program.

The Associated Press reported that Weiss is calling for a new direction at the storied news magazine. The New York Times described the changes as a major shakeup for the program. The moves represent significant personnel changes at one of CBS's flagship news programs.

cards.headline: Hacks Ends Five-Season Run With Series Finale on HBO Max
cards.teaser: The comedy series starring Jean Smart concluded with a finale that brought Deborah Vance and Ava Daniels to Paris.
cards.body:
Hacks aired its series finale on HBO Max, ending the five-season run of the streaming comedy starring Jean Smart as comedian Deborah Vance and Hannah Einbinder as her writer Ava Daniels. The finale took the characters to Paris and included scenes of the pair workshopping jokes together.

In the closing minutes, Vance and Daniels returned to the collaborative dynamic that had been less present in the final season. Producers and stars discussed the finale and its ending for the two main characters. The series creators said they needed to raise the stakes in the final episode.

cards.headline: The White Lotus Films Scenes at Cannes Film Festival Venue
cards.teaser: Production on the fourth season of The White Lotus moved to Cannes, where filming took place at the Palais des Festivals.
cards.body:
Mike White's anthology series The White Lotus moved production to the Palais des Festivals in Cannes after completing filming at Chateau de la Messardiere in Saint-Tropez. The cast for season four includes Laura Dern, Steve Coogan, Ari Graynor, and Max Greenfield.

The production took over the festival venue to film what appear to be significant scenes, including a recreation of a dramatic Cannes closing night event.

cards.headline: Tito Double P Releases Second Solo Album Acomodo
cards.teaser: The Mexican music artist released a 23-track album as his sophomore solo project.
cards.body:
Tito Double P released his second solo album, titled Acomodo, featuring 23 tracks. The project represents the Mexican music star's continued development as a solo artist following his debut release.

The expansive album showcases Tito Double P's work in the Mexican music genre. The release follows his first solo effort and marks a progression in his individual career separate from collaborative projects.

cards.headline: Jay Wheeler Returns With Album La Voz Favorita
cards.teaser: The Puerto Rican singer released a new album exploring trap and reggaeton styles.
cards.body:
Puerto Rican artist Jay Wheeler released La Voz Favorita, an album that traces his musical roots across trap and reggaeton genres. Wheeler has earned the nickname Latin Music's Favorite Voice from fans.

The album represents a return for the singer to the styles that shaped his

hero.headline: US and Iran near agreement to extend ceasefire, reopen Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
The United States and Iran are close to finalizing a memorandum of understanding that would extend their ceasefire by 60 days and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though some disagreements remain unresolved.

Vice President JD Vance said Thursday that negotiators were "very close" to completing the agreement but still working through final details. "We're still going back and forth on nuclear stuff," Vance said, indicating that disputes over Tehran's nuclear program continue to be a sticking point.

According to US officials, negotiators have already reached agreement on the framework of a 60-day ceasefire extension. However, the deal still requires final approval from President Trump and Iran's leadership before it becomes official.

The tentative memorandum addresses multiple pressing issues. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route that has been closed during the conflict, would reopen under the agreement. The deal would also establish a framework for broader negotiations on Tehran's nuclear program, a long-standing concern for the Trump administration.

Pakistan has been playing an active role in mediating talks between the two sides. Pakistan's army chief led a delegation to Tehran to convey messages from Washington, while Pakistan's prime minister traveled to Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Turkey to build regional support for a peace agreement.

Karoline Leavitt, the White House press secretary, said on Wednesday that Washington remained engaged in negotiations despite earlier denials of a formal extension request. She stated that a second round of negotiations would "very likely" be held in Islamabad and that the White House feels "good about the prospects of a deal."

The current ceasefire was set to expire on April 22. Both sides have been engaged in indirect talks aimed at extending the truce, with continued exchanges of messages between Washington and Tehran even after previous rounds of negotiations broke down.

Trump and his advisers have previously believed they were close to a final agreement at earlier stages of the conflict, though those negotiations ultimately stalled. A final comprehensive agreement addressing Trump's nuclear demands would require further intensive negotiations beyond the initial memorandum of understanding.

The three-month conflict has strained regional stability and disrupted global shipping routes. Reports from the region suggest both sides favor prolonging the truce, though significant work remains to resolve underlying disputes.

The tentative agreement represents the most substantial diplomatic breakthrough since the conflict began. However, nothing is considered official until formally announced by the White House. Both sides continue intensive discussions to finalize the remaining details before the ceasefire expires.

cards.headline: Trump administration bars Americans exposed to Ebola from returning to US
cards.teaser: A 50-bed quarantine facility in Kenya will house Americans exposed to the virus starting this week.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is building a quarantine and treatment facility in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, rather than allowing them to return home. The 50-bed field hospital is set to open Friday.

Some experts have criticized this approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning to the US could undermine treatment efforts for the outbreak.

cards.headline: Police respond to swatting call at Justice Amy Coney Barrett's home
cards.teaser: Law enforcement received a report of gunshots at the Supreme Court justice's Virginia residence.
cards.body:
Supreme Court Justice Amy Coney Barrett was the victim of a swatting call at her Virginia home. Police radio traffic shows law enforcement received a call for a suspicious noise of gunshots at Barrett's suburban Virginia address.

The dispatcher warned responding officers shortly afterward that a high priority resident of the county lived there and that the report may not be authentic.

cards.headline: White House creates website highlighting unauthorized immigrant arrests
cards.teaser: The site uses space imagery to display enforcement data.
cards.body:
The White House launched a space-themed website that displays arrests of immigrants unauthorized to live in the US. The website, launched on Thursday, opens with a crawl similar to the one seen in the Star Wars franchise, with blocks of text.

The site mocks the idea of the US retaining secrets involving alien encounters while highlighting immigration enforcement activity.

cards.headline: Michigan Gov. Whitmer backtracks on 2028 presidential run comment
cards.teaser: The term-limited governor has been viewed as a potential Democratic candidate.
cards.body: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer has walked back earlier remarks suggesting she would not run for president in 2028. As a term-limited governor following two election victories in the competitive swing state, Whitmer has emerged as a potential Democratic presidential candidate for the next election cycle.

cards.headline: AI, crypto, and pro-Israel groups spend heavily against congressional candidates
cards.teaser: The spending has targeted members of Congress and candidates in primary races.
cards.body:
AI companies, the cryptocurrency industry, and pro-Israel groups are spending at unprecedented levels to defeat their least favored members of Congress and congressional candidates. Pro-Israel groups spent nearly $8 million to oust GOP Rep. Thomas Massie in Kentucky's 4th District, helping to fuel the most expensive House primary in American history.

Crypto-aligned Protect Progress was by far the largest spender in several races. The volume of spending has the potential to end political careers and stop political movements.

cards.headline: Sen. Collins responds to challenger's Iraq war criticism
cards.teaser: The Maine senator defended her record after a Democratic challenger cited her support for military intervention.
cards.body:
Sen. Susan Collins hit back at a comment from the top Democratic challenger in Maine's Senate race about her past support of US military foreign intervention. Graham Platner, a Marine veteran and oyster farmer, told The New York Times earlier this month that the incumbent senator voted to send him to Iraq.

Collins responded by noting that Platner was not drafted. Platner is challenging Collins in the upcoming Senate race.
